attention_patterns.note: two short ticks, spaced; the second gap ends the pattern.
three short ticks; the last silence is the tail.
one long buzz; the following silence is the tail.
each buzz grows; the final silence is the tail.
two beats, closer first gap; the second silence is the tail.
two beats with a long first gap; the second silence is the tail.
a declining run that ends on the tail silence.

rationale.word_gap_ms: The silence between two words of one utterance (inside a word the cell gap is the wearer's pace). 520 ms is about a quarter longer than the 420 ms default cell gap - above the ~20% Weber fraction for empty tactile intervals, so a word boundary is felt as a boundary at the default pace - and 30 ms under the 550 ms prefix breath, the one silence that already means 'a boundary between events' (who, then why), so a word boundary never outranks it. It cannot read as an ending because nothing ends on silence any more: only end-of-message ends an utterance (plan s4 invariant 2). Known limit, to validate on the feel-tool: the gap is a constant while the pace is tunable 250-700 ms, so at paces of 520 ms and slower the word boundary is no longer longer than a cell gap; if slow readers need it, v5 defines the word gap relative to the pace.
rationale.working_every_ms: How often a device repeats the processing pattern on its own clock while a body is pending (architecture s5.1). 2000 ms is the relay's old cadence (PROCESSING_EVERY_S = 2.0) and the plan's '~2 s' (s4 invariant 3: waiting is legible). The pattern itself lasts 910 ms, so each repeat is followed by about a second of silence - a pulse, not a drone. The reference renderer models the header part only (one pattern); the repeats are device time, not utterance time.
rationale.conformance_tolerance_ms: Per-beat |delta t| a real renderer may drift from the reference timeline and still conform (dot mask and buzz length must match exactly). 10 ms matches tools/qemu_timeline.py's HAP differ and sits well under the shortest silence in the spec (the 30 ms slot gap), so a tolerance can never hide a merged or missing beat.
rationale.kinds: Kind -> arrival cue and prefix tail. Both are the same pattern per kind on purpose: the cue a wearer feels mid-read ('something of this kind is waiting') and the tail after the name mark ('this is why I am speaking') are one vocabulary item each, so there are four things to learn, not eight. prefix.tails is the firmware's older view of the same mapping and must agree with it; validate() enforces that.
rationale.profiles.single_actuator: A phone has one motor, so a cell is six time slots in column order (dots 1, 2, 3, then 4, 5, 6): a raised dot is a 50 ms pulse in its slot, an absent dot is 50 ms of silence; 30 ms of silence follows every slot but the last and 80 ms more follows the third slot (the column break), so the cell's duration is fixed at 6 x 50 + 5 x 30 + 80 = 530 ms whatever the letter - the letter lives in where the pulses fall, not in how many there are. 530 ms is about 2.2 x the mean chord cell (244 ms over the alphabet) and 1.5 x the heaviest (350 ms), the 'roughly twice' architecture s5.2 budgets for. The 50 ms pulse is the shortest buzz already in the vocabulary (ramp-up's first beat, cell_base_ms); the 30/80 ms gaps make the column break (110 ms of silence) almost four times the in-column gap. All three numbers are provisional until validated on the feel-tool with braille readers: the trade is legibility of pulse position against the time budget, and a slower slot (e.g. 70/40/100) is the first thing to try if positions blur.

note: Feel-tool page affordances only - the band fires patterns immediately, does not loop them, and tunes cell gap in its own config within the same envelope. spell_max_letters caps the page's spell box; the firmware accepts up to 16 (HAPTIC_OUT_MAX_WORD_LEN) so the band is never the weaker player. These two numbers are intentionally different and are NOT the same setting: spell_max_letters (12) is a page affordance that limits what the spell box headlines for the wearer, while HAPTIC_OUT_MAX_WORD_LEN (16) is the firmware's hard ceiling on word length the band will actually play. Do not unify them - the asymmetry is deliberate, and the drift guard (tools/haptic_timing.py --verify) treats the generated feel-tool JS block and the firmware header as separate consumers of the same spec, each free to use different UI vs. runtime limits.
